facts.fact: Wingu Africa presented to Djibouti's communications minister an internet exchange point (IXP) that is already in service within its data centre in Djibouti, per the Agence Djiboutienne d'Information report of the 28 September 2026 meeting; no member count or city beyond the country is given.

slug: 2026-07-13 Djibouti Seeks ITU, Smart Africa Support for Telecoms and AI Development

facts.fact: We Are Tech Africa states that Djibouti operates three data centres and an Internet Exchange Point (IXP); the exchange is not named and no members or city are given. Dated by the article's publication date, 2026-07-13.

note: Regional Starlink article; exchanges named (NAPAfrica, JINX, KIXP, IXPN Lagos) are in other countries and Djibouti appears only in a Starlink availability table.

facts.fact: Wingu Africa says it has launched the AMS-IX Djibouti Internet exchange in partnership with AMS-IX, expanding on the existing DjIX infrastructure; no member count given; the article gives no launch date, so as_of is the article's published date (2025-06-06).

Wingu Africa refers to an existing DjIX exchange infrastructure in Djibouti, which AMS-IX Djibouti expands upon; no members or traffic given; no date given, so as_of is the article's published date (2025-06-06).

note: ADDIX is in Ethiopia and is not a fact for DJI; Wingu's Djibouti data centres and 12 submarine cables are other classes.
Funding story; names ADDIX (Ethiopia) only and no exchange point in Djibouti.

facts.fact: The French Treasury note says the data centre operator also runs the Djibouti Internet Exchange (DjIX), a neutral and independent exchange point.
AMS-IX says the Djibouti Internet Exchange (DjIX) is in operation and becomes AMS-IX Djibouti under a partnership with Wingu Africa.
AMS-IX says peak traffic growth at DjIX is attributed to increased traffic by several content delivery networks located at AMS-IX Djibouti, none named.
AMS-IX says DjIX's peak traffic is currently four times that of a year ago.
The African IXP Association's undated list of exchange points, retrieved 2026-11-09, names for Djibouti: AMS-IX Djibouti.

note: Names the Djibouti Internet Exchange and a 2023 AMS-IX agreement to replace it, but does not say networks exchange traffic there; hopes of Facebook, Google or Amazon are aspirations.
An exchange initiative with the sovereign fund is said not to have started construction; no exchange in service.
